results.title: Nebius Raises On-Demand GPU Prices Up to 21% From October 1: What an H100 Hour Now Costs | ServerCalc
results.author: ServerCalc Editorial
highlights:
# Nebius Raises On-Demand GPU Prices Up to 21% From October 1: What an H100 Hour Now Costs

Nebius lifted pay-as-you-go GPU rates up to 21% on October 1 — H100 to $4.50 an hour, B300 to $9.50 — the second rise since spring as AI capacity sells out.

October 12, 2026 ServerCalc Editorial 5 min read

The capacity squeeze that has been pushing up VPS prices all year sits at the other end of the market too, on the GPU servers that AI workloads run on. One of the larger listed GPU clouds, Nebius, has just moved its on-demand prices again — the second time it has done so since the spring — and the new rates are a useful marker for anyone pricing an AI server rather than a plain VPS.

## What changed

From October 1, 2026, Nebius raised its on-demand, pay-as-you-go rates across its four current Nvidia platforms. On its own published price list the per-GPU-hour numbers now read: H100 NVLink at $4.50, up from $3.85 (about 17%); H200 NVLink at $5.40, up from $4.50 (20%); B200 NVLink at $8.50, up from $7.15 (about 19%); and B300 NVLink at $9.50, up from $7.85 (21%). CPU-only servers were caught in the same round — the AMD EPYC Genoa vCPU now lists at $0.015 per CPU-hour, roughly a quarter more than before. Separately, from October 8 the provider moved preemptible capacity for these platforms onto dynamic spot pricing, so the cheap interruptible tier no longer has a fixed rate.

These are list prices for on-demand use. Committed and reserved terms are quoted separately and run well below the hourly rate; the increase lands hardest on buyers who pay by the hour with no commitment.

...

Figures in this piece are from Nebius's published compute pricing page and from reporting by The Motley Fool on the October 1 increase, cross-checked against the provider's own effective-date notice.

**Spheron Network**.

---

Nebius raised H100 prices 17% and H200 prices 20% on September 17, effective October 1. H100 and H200 are two of the GPUs most teams rent for LLM training and inference. If you had an instance running under the old contract, the new rate applies to it now, not at renewal.

You did not choose that new rate. A fixed-term contract works like this: the provider sets a new price, and every running instance inherits it on the provider's schedule. Per-minute billing works differently. You pay whatever rate is posted right now, for the minutes you actually use, and nothing carries forward past that.

On Spheron, that means:

- You see the live rate before every deployment, not on an annual renewal notice.
- You can move a workload to a different GPU or provider the same day if a better rate shows up elsewhere.
- Reserved pricing still exists if you want a fixed rate locked in. On-demand just stays the default instead of something you have to opt into.

As of October 6, 2026, on-demand H100 starts at $2.01/hr on the marketplace, and spot H200 starts at $3.31/hr. Spot means the rate for using capacity that is free right now, and it runs below the on-demand rate. These are live marketplace numbers and can vary by region.

A fixed-term contract can raise your rate without warning. Check current on-demand and spot rates on the marketplace before your next renewal

results.title: The same H100 can cost $0.79 or $12.29 an hour. Both are list prices, in the same month. | Compute Stacker
results.author: Compute Stacker
highlights:
# The same H100 can cost $0.79 or $12.29 an hour. Both are list prices, in the same month. | Compute Stacker · LinkedIn · 2026-10-15T00:00:00+00:00

**Compute Stacker**.

---

The same H100 can cost $0.79 or $12.29 an hour. Both are list prices, in the same month.

The low end is Nebius preemptible, under its new dynamic spot pricing that started October 8. The high end is Azure's on-demand ND96isr H100 v5, at $98.32 per 8-GPU node.

Four purchase types, same chip:

- Preemptible and spot: Nebius from $0.79 (a floor, not a fixed price), CoreWeave spot at $19.71 per 8-GPU node, or $2.46 per GPU
- On-demand: $3.99 at Lambda, $4.50 at Nebius, $6.16 at CoreWeave, $12.29 at Azure
- Reserved: AWS Capacity Blocks moved to $5.970 per GPU-hour on October 7
- Committed: CoreWeave advertises up to 60% off on-demand, with no published tiers

The cheap tiers carry conditions. Preemptible capacity can be reclaimed, so it fits checkpointed work, not a production endpoint. Nebius's spot price can now change every 15 minutes, including during a run. Committed rates need a contract.

What this means in practice: before comparing two providers, make sure you're comparing the same purchase type. A spot rate against an on-demand rate is a 3x gap that tells you nothing about which provider is cheaper.

And re-check on the day you budget. Nebius changed its pricing twice in eight days.

results.title: Nebius quietly changed how it prices preemptible GPUs on October 8, a week after raising on-demand rates. | Devanshu Rajput
results.author: Devanshu Rajput
highlights:
# Nebius quietly changed how it prices preemptible GPUs on October 8, a week after raising on-demand rates. | Devanshu Rajput · LinkedIn · 2026-10-15T00:00:00+00:00

**Devanshu Rajput**: Growth & Marketing Intern @ ComputeStacker | Content Marketing | SEO | Market Research | Social Media | AI & Technology.

---

Nebius quietly changed how it prices preemptible GPUs on October 8, a week after raising on-demand rates.

Preemptible H100, H200, B200, B300 and RTX PRO 6000 moved from fixed rates to dynamic spot pricing. The published number is now a floor, not a price.

For the H100, that means "$2.15 per GPU-hour" became "from $0.79." The B300 went from $4.30 to a floor of $0.99.

The mechanics matter more than the floor. Nebius says spot prices move with capacity, utilisation and demand, can change as often as every 15 minutes, and can change during use. The ceiling is one cent below the on-demand rate for the same capacity.

So on an H100 the possible range is now $0.79 to $4.49 an hour, on the same chip, in the same region, depending on when you run.

That's a different planning problem from a fixed preemptible rate. You can model a fixed rate in a budget. A range this wide needs you to watch the actual price, not the rate card.

Two things worth knowing: this is the second Nebius change this month, after the October 1 on-demand increase, and the H100 is in one region only, eu-north1.

Picking one "cheap" neocloud over the hyperscalers has a catch: when that single provider hits its own capacity wall, you inherit its price hikes too. CoreWeave just showed exactly how that plays out.

Spheron is a marketplace that aggregates GPU supply from certified Tier 3+ data centers worldwide, not a single cloud provider, so no one partner's price hike becomes your problem. On-demand H100s start at $2.01/hr today, no contract required, with reserved and spot options if your usage pattern is more predictable.

results.title: GPU clouds with per-second billing and no monthly base fee
results.author: Dora Pruteanu
highlights:
In short

Lyceum and Exoscale bill GPU compute by the second with no monthly base fee; Hyperstack bills per minute, and Nebius, OVHcloud, Scaleway and Verda list hourly rates. Hetzner's GEX line is dedicated servers with a one-time setup fee. Between jobs, storage and reserved IPs still cost money. Lyceum's and Verda's rates were read on 14 October 2026, the other providers' values on 24 September 2026.

...

- Lyceum's on-demand GPU virtual machines are billed per second with no subscription and no monthly minimum, with 1, 2, 4 or 8 GPUs per instance; the H100 lists at $3.49 per GPU-hour, against $4.50 at Nebius (Lyceum read 14 October 2026).
- Exoscale also bills resources by the second with no up-front costs.
- Hetzner's GPU offering is the GEX line of dedicated servers with monthly and hourly rates plus a one-time setup fee, not per-second cloud VMs.
- A stopped instance still costs money: OVHcloud bills the public IPv4 option at €0.0027 per hour, about €1.97 per month, from October 2026, and Verda lists NVMe storage at $0.20 per GiB-month.
- No monthly base fee appears on any of the eight providers' pricing pages; Nebius states a $25 minimum first payment.

...

A team that wants to pay only for the seconds a GPU runs can use Lyceum's on-demand GPU virtual machines, billed per second with no subscription [1] and launched with 1, 2, 4 or 8 GPUs per instance [2]. Lyceum's billing has no monthly minimum, and prepaid credits do not expire [3]. On its on-demand table, read 14 October 2026, the H100 lists at $3.49 per GPU-hour, the A100 at $1.89 and the L40S at $1.45 [1].

| Provider | On-demand price per GPU-hour | Minimum term | Billing unit | GPUs per instance |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Lyceum | H100 $3.49; A100 $1.89; L40S $1.45 | None | Per second | 1, 2, 4 or 8 |
| Exoscale | – | None; no long-term commitments | Per second | – |
| Hetzner | – | One-time setup fee; monthly term | Monthly or hourly (dedicated server) | 1 |
| Hyperstack | Hourly list per GPU model, billed by the minute | – | Per minute | – |
| Nebius | H100 $4.50; H200 $5.40; L40S from $1.55 [4] | $25 minimum first payment | Per GPU-hour listed | – |
| OVHcloud | A100 $3.07 [5] | – | Per hour | 1, 2 or 4 |
| Scaleway | L4 €0.79; H100 and L40S – [6] | – | Per hour | 1, 2, 4 or 8 |
| Verda | H100 $4.13; H200 $5.38; A100 $1.98 (read 14 October 2026) [7] | – | Per hour | 1, 2, 4 or 8 |

...

The billing unit divides the field into three groups. Lyceum and Exoscale bill by the second [1]; Exoscale's pricing page states that resources are billed by the second, with no up-front costs and no long-term commitments. [8] Hyperstack bills per minute; its pricing FAQ states that the on-demand prepaid platform bills for each minute of use. [9] Hetzner's GEX line consists of dedicated GPU servers with monthly pricing and a one-time setup fee, not per-second virtual machines. [10] Nebius, OVHcloud, Scaleway and Verda publish per-hour rates and make no per-second claim on their pricing pages. [4] [6] [7]

...

No monthly base fee appears on any of the eight pricing pages, and Lyceum states that its billing has no monthly minimum. [3] Two minimums do appear: Hetzner's GEX servers carry a one-time setup fee, and Nebius states a $25 minimum for the first payment. [4] Readers who need a partial node rather than a full eight-GPU server can compare per-GPU rates in the separate guide to partial-node rentals.

...

1. Between-jobs costs against idle time: price storage and reserved IPs from the list above before comparing GPU rates.
2. Contract shape: Hetzner's GEX line is a dedicated server on monthly terms with a one-time setup fee, not a per-second cloud VM. Commitment pricing trades flexibility for rate: Lyceum agrees commitment pricing per contract for reserved GPUs and clusters, [1] Nebius states commitment discounts of up to 35% below on-demand rates, [4] and Verda lists 2% off on-demand at one month rising to 25% at two years. [7]

...

Do these GPU clouds charge a monthly base fee?

No monthly base fee appears on any of the eight pricing pages read on 24 September 2026 (Lyceum's and Verda's on 14 October 2026). The closest things to a fixed charge are Hetzner's one-time setup fee on its GEX dedicated servers and Nebius's $25 minimum first payment, which is a payment threshold rather than a recurring fee.

| Service or model | Published pricing structure | What to verify |
| --- | --- | --- |

See Runpod pricing, whose page showed a pricing update dated 8 October 2026. |
| Runpod Serverless | Usage-billed inference workers rather than a continuously rented instance. | Worker startup and idle behavior, execution duration, concurrency, cold starts, storage, and egress. The page does not establish a universal per-token rate. |
| Runpod Clusters | Multi-node GPU capacity for jobs that need several machines. | Node count, interconnect, orchestration, reservation terms, and storage. Cluster pricing cannot be compared directly with a single-GPU serverless request. |
| Nebius HGX H100 | $3.85 per GPU-hour on demand; from $0.79 per GPU-hour preemptible. | These are examples shown on the page accessed 13 October 2026. Confirm region, exact configuration, interruption policy, and current inventory at Nebius GPU pricing. |
| Nebius HGX H200 | $4.50 per GPU-hour on demand; from $0.79 per GPU-hour preemptible. | The preemptible figure is a starting rate, not a guaranteed recurring price. Nebius says spot rates can change with capacity, cluster utilization, demand, and customer pricing preferences, potentially every 15 minutes. |
| CoreWeave | The pricing page separates on-demand, spot, and inference-platform products. | Product eligibility and billing basis before comparing an inference-platform rate with a general GPU-hour. See CoreWeave pricing. |

Nebius also says long-term, stable workloads may qualify for usage commitments that reduce rates. The discount percentage and commitment terms are not stated on the cited page; obtain them in the commercial quote rather than assuming that a public rate applies.
